Today pairs your two projects with a strong theory thread. Diffusion models sample the 2D Heisenberg (O(3)) lattice model

arXiv · statistical mechanics · 8/10

The abstract reports a score-based diffusion model trained on the 2D classical Heisenberg model, with multiscale sampling that modestly improves accuracy and cost. It also introduces Schwinger-Dyson (Stein) diagnostics for two-point correlations. This likely connects to your Glauber/Kawasaki MC and autoencoder pipeline as a generative alternative. Check whether it works near criticality, where correlation lengths grow.

Melt-pool classifier benchmarks transfer learning on NIST AMMT images

arXiv · AM monitoring & physics · 6/10

The abstract reports binary normal/abnormal classification on 1,200 balanced melt-pool images from Ni625 on NIST AMMT, comparing ResNet50, EfficientNetB0 and MobileNetV2 against Random Forests. It also weighs inference time against open-architecture machine constraints. The 80/20 stratified random split is the red flag you track: check for per-build leakage, and whether 'abnormal' is a ground-truth label or a parameter proxy.

Mg impurities cut Ising-like Co chains into finite segments

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 7/10

The abstract reports neutron scattering on quasi-1D Ising-like antiferromagnet Ba(Co1-xMgx)2V2O8, where non-magnetic Mg fragments the chains into finite segments. This is a real-crystal view of finite-size effects, which is close to the logic behind your finite-size scaling. It is an antiferromagnet, so check how much transfers to a ferromagnet with easy-axis anisotropy.

Torque magnetometry plus DFT reveal NiPS3 anisotropy beyond XY/XXZ

arXiv · ML materials discovery · 6/10

The abstract reports high-field torque magnetometry showing an anisotropic response beyond standard XY or XXZ models. Relativistic DFT and magnetic force response theory build an effective spin Hamiltonian, with dipole interaction playing a key role. It bears on your open anisotropy gap and on the 'Ising' easy-axis evidence red flag. Check how the exchange and anisotropy terms were separated.

MLFFs reach near-full OMat24 accuracy using under 1% of the data

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 6/10

The abstract reports MACE models trained on 6.5M atoms (under 1% of OMat24) approaching the full-data model within tens of meV/Å in forces. The selection methods tested are random, DIRECT clustering and a new EnvTok local-environment method. This likely supports small-data and active-selection strategies for your pipeline. Check whether magnetic properties were evaluated at all.

Theoretical Physics

Ten-loop RG functions for the 3D O(N) model via GPU integration

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 7/10

The abstract reports extending fixed-dimension RG functions from eight to ten loops (β to eleven) using tropical Monte Carlo on GPUs. In plain words, these series pin down critical exponents of Ising/Heisenberg-class transitions, the universality data your finite-size scaling is checked against. Check the resulting exponent precision versus Monte Carlo and bootstrap values.

Exact high-temperature expansion of the inverse-square Ising chain in a field

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 6/10

The abstract reports exact field-dependent coefficients for this long-range chain, which has a Thouless transition, plus a finite-ring reconstruction. Exact results like this are useful benchmarks for MC and finite-size methods. Check how it treats ring-size dependence.

Quanta Magazine · Physics · 6/10

The Quanta piece says gravity can 'collapse the dimensions of space,' as in holography, where a gravitational world is described by a lower-dimensional theory without gravity. All derivations of the Born rule assume probability, APS analysis finds

APS Physics · 6/10

The Born rule says quantum probabilities come from squared amplitudes. The APS summary reports that all major derivations quietly assume something probabilistic, so they don't explain probability from non-probabilistic ground. Check which derivations are covered and whether the authors argue it's fatal.
